mainTopic: How a slave gains freedom: masters' actions that prove freedom, a dying master's instructions, a slave made ownerless, and a partner's trick to avoid freeing a slave.
overview: The amud asks when a master's actions prove he freed his slave. רבי יוחנן challenges רבי זירא's ruling about a slave who marries a free woman in front of his master. The גמרא answers that the master himself married the slave off, and it explains a ברייתא about a master betrothing his own שפחה as a debate over wording. Next, רבי יהושע בן לוי says a slave who puts on תפילין in front of his master goes free, and רבה בר רב שילא limits this to a case where the master put the תפילין on him. Two students then bring different reports of רבי יוחנן's ruling about a dying master's words regarding his maidservant: רב דימי and רב שמואל בר יהודה. אמימר rules that a slave whose master was מפקיר him has no תקנה, and he defends this against רב אשי by calling רב דימי's report a mistake. רבינא, relying on רב דימי, tells slaves who were sold to a non-Jew to get a גט שחרור from the sons of their first masters, and the הלכה follows רבינא. The amud ends with a partner who gave his share of a half-freed slave to his minor son to avoid freeing him, and רב פפא begins explaining how the trick will backfire. The explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ruling: the slave goes free
steps.stepSummary: These are the closing words of רבי זירא's ruling: a slave who married a free woman in front of his master goes free.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...he goes out to freedom.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of a ruling that started before this section. רבי זירא said a slave who marries a free woman in front of his master becomes free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the master watched and did not object. A slave is not allowed to marry a free Jewish woman, so his silence shows he must have freed the slave. This ruling is what רבי יוחנן is about to attack.

keyTerms.meaning: He goes out to freedom; the slave becomes free
A non-Jewish slave owned by a Jew

phrases.english: he goes out to freedom.
phrases.notes: This finishes רבי זירא's ruling from just before: a slave who married a free woman in front of his master.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ruling of רבי זירא that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave who marries a free woman in front of his master becomes free.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even a master's own betrothal doesn't free her
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן is amazed at the ruling. He cites a ברייתא where the חכמים say a master who writes a שטר אירוסין to his own maidservant does not betroth her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: You hold that much?! But I learn: if someone writes a betrothal document to his maidservant, רבי מאיר says she is betrothed, and the Sages say she is not betrothed!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks רבי זירא's ruling with a ברייתא. In it, the חכמים say that even when a master tries to marry his own maidservant, she is not freed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the master himself writes a betrothal document to his שפחה, which is a much stronger act than quietly watching. Yet the חכמים say it does not count as freeing her, so she is not betrothed. All the more so, a master merely standing by at his slave's wedding should not free the slave.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you really hold so much? An expression of surprise at an extreme ruling
But I learn: introduces a ברייתא as a challenge
A document used to betroth a woman
A non-Jewish maidservant
She is betrothed

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge comes from the חכמים, not from רבי מאיר. The חכמים say a master's own betrothal document does not free his maidservant, and that is what clashes with רבי זירא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
phrases.notes: He is speaking to רבי זירא.

phrases.english: You hold that much in your hand?!
But I learn:
one who writes a betrothal document for his maidservant,
Rabbi Meir says: she is betrothed,
and the Sages say: she is not betrothed!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כָּל כָּךְ יֵשׁ בְּיָדְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just completed in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's ruling that a slave marrying in front of his master goes free.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even the master's own betrothal of his maidservant does not free her (per the חכמים), then his passive presence at his slave's marriage surely should not free the slave.

steps.title: The master himself married off the slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי זירא means a case where the master actively married the slave off. This matches how רבה בר רב שילא explained the case of תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה בר רב שילא said, it is a case where his master put תפילין on him. Here too, it is a case where his master married him off to a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי זירא by narrowing his case. The master did not just watch; he himself arranged the slave's marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר רב שילא explained a similar ruling about תפילין (brought in steps 6–8) as a case where the master himself put the תפילין on the slave. The same move works here. A master who actively marries his slave to a free woman would not do so unless he had freed him, so this clearly shows freedom.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too: applies one explanation to another case
Married him off to a woman
Leather boxes with פסוקים inside; a slave wearing them in front of his master is discussed in steps 6–8 as a sign of freedom

phrases.english: As Rabba bar Rav Sheila said —
where his master put tefillin on him;
here too —
where his master married him off to a woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's challenge by narrowing רבי זירא's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) by comparison to an earlier explanation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי זירא seemed to mean the master merely watched the marriage happen.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי זירא means the master himself married the slave off, which clearly shows he freed him.

steps.title: Would a master avoid a sin for his slave but commit it himself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if a master would not commit an איסור by marrying his slave to a free woman, surely he would not commit one himself by marrying his maidservant unfreed. So why do the חכמים say she is not betrothed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there such a thing, that for his slave he would not commit a prohibition, but he himself would commit a prohibition?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. The same logic should also make the master's betrothal of his maidservant prove that he freed her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer assumed a master would not break an איסור by marrying his unfreed slave to a free woman. If so, he also would not break an איסור himself by betrothing his own unfreed maidservant. So in the ברייתא his betrothal should show he freed her, and the חכמים's ruling that she is not betrothed is hard to understand.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there such a thing? A rhetorical challenge
A prohibition, a sin
Does, commits

phrases.english: And is there such a thing
that for his slave he would not commit a prohibition,
phrases.notes: This means marrying his slave to a free woman without freeing him first.

phrases.english: but he himself would commit a prohibition?!
phrases.notes: This means betrothing his own maidservant without freeing her first.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי דִּלְעַבְדֵּיהּ לָא מִעֲבַד לֵיהּ אִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in step 3 leaves the ברייתא from step 2 still unexplained.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation in step 3, as it relates to the חכמים's view in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If we assume a master avoids sin for his slave, we must also assume he avoids sin himself. So his betrothal of his maidservant should prove he freed her, against the חכמים.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about one document meant to free and betroth at once
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains the ברייתא as a case where the master said 'go free with this and be betrothed with this.' The argument is only whether these words can free her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: What are we dealing with here? A case where he said to her: 'Go free with this and be betrothed with this.' רבי מאיר holds that this wording contains a wording of freeing, and the רבנן hold that this wording does not contain a wording of freeing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the last question by explaining the ברייתא as a special case. The master tried to use one document both to free his maidservant and to betroth her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody suspects the master of betrothing his maidservant without freeing her; he clearly meant to free her. The only question is whether this document's wording can actually free her. רבי מאיר says yes, so she is betrothed. The רבנן say no, so she is still a שפחה and cannot be betrothed.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Introduces a narrowed explanation of a source
Go free with this and be betrothed with this
Wording that frees a slave

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees a master would not marry his slave to a free woman, or betroth his own maidservant, without freeing them first. רבי מאיר and the רבנן only argue about whether one document can free and betroth at the same time.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
With what are we dealing here —
where he said to her:
"Go free with this and be betrothed with this";
phrases.notes: "This" is the one document he handed her.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:
this wording contains a wording of freeing,
and the Rabbis hold:
this wording does not contain a wording of freeing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 by explaining the ברייתא from step 2 as a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (הכא במאי עסקינן) so the argument is about wording, not suspicion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים seemed to hold that a master's betrothal of his maidservant does not show he freed her, as if he might sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: The master clearly intended to free her. The חכמים simply hold that this wording in the betrothal document cannot free her, so she remains a שפחה and is not betrothed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רבי זירא's ruling. Everyone agrees a master is not suspected of sinning, so his active marrying off of his slave proves the slave is free.

steps.title: A slave who puts on תפילין in front of his master goes free
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that a slave who puts on תפילין in front of his master goes free.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: A slave who put on תפילין in front of his master goes free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling: if a slave puts on תפילין while his master watches, the slave becomes free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave is not obligated in תפילין, so putting them on is something a free Jew does. If the master sees it and does not object, it seems the slave is already free.

keyTerms.meaning: Leather boxes with פסוקים inside, worn on the arm and head
Goes out to freedom; becomes a free person
In front of his master

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
A slave who put on tefillin in front of his master
goes out to freedom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the תפילין ruling that the earlier answer (Step 3) pointed to as a parallel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave who puts on תפילין in front of his master is freed.

steps.title: A ברייתא says putting on תפילין does not free the slave
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists actions done in front of the master, including putting on תפילין, and says none of them free the slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If his master borrowed money from him, or his master made him a manager over his property, or he put on תפילין in front of his master, or he read three פסוקים in shul in front of his master, he does not go free!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע בן לוי with a ברייתא that says outright that putting on תפילין in front of the master does not free a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the actions in the list look like things a free man does. Still, the ברייתא says the slave stays a slave. This directly clashes with רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A manager or caretaker over someone's property
Borrowed from him

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If his master borrowed from him,
or his master made him a manager,
or he put on tefillin in front of his master,
or he read three verses
in the synagogue in front of his master,
this one does not go out to freedom!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling that putting on תפילין in front of the master frees the slave
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא names the exact same case and rules the opposite: the slave is not freed.

steps.title: It means the master put the תפילין on him
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב שילא explains that רבי יהושע בן לוי is talking about a case where the master himself put the תפילין on the slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב שילא said: It is talking about when his master put the תפילין on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing רבי יהושע בן לוי's case: the master actively put the תפילין on the slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the slave put them on by himself, and the master only watched, so he stays a slave. But if the master himself puts the תפילין on him, that shows the master already freed him, since he would not otherwise do this.

keyTerms.meaning: When his master put them on him

steps.whatToRemember: Watching the slave do a free man's מצוה does not free him; the master actively doing it for him does.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Sheila said:
When his master put tefillin on him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע בן לוי seemed to mean any slave who puts on תפילין while his master watches.
steps.terutzMaskana: He means only when the master himself put the תפילין on the slave; the ברייתא is about the slave doing it himself.

steps.title: A dying master says not to enslave his maidservant
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that רבי יוחנן ruled: if a dying man says his heirs should not enslave a certain maidservant, the court forces them to write her a document of freedom.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone said when he was dying, 'So-and-so my maidservant, do not enslave her after my death,' the court forces the heirs to write her a document of freedom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: what happens when a dying master gives instructions about his maidservant. This is רב דימי's version of רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The master did not free her himself. But רבי יוחנן reads 'do not enslave her' as a request to free her, so the heirs are made to do it with a proper document.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
At the time of his death
The court forces
A document that frees a slave
Heirs

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came,
phrases.notes: He came from ארץ ישראל to בבל and brought rulings from there.

phrases.english: he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who said at the time of his death,
"So-and-so, my maidservant,
they should not enslave her after my death" —
we force the heirs
and they write her a document of freedom.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about a dying master's words regarding his maidservant.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a dying master says not to enslave his maidservant, the heirs are forced to write her a document of freedom.

steps.title: Don't you agree her children stay slaves?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי and רבי אסי challenge רבי יוחנן: don't you agree her children are slaves? That would show the master never meant to free her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי אסי said to him: רבי, don't you agree that her children are slaves?
steps.whatsHappening: Two students challenge רבי יוחנן's ruling by pointing to the status of the maidservant's children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her children stay slaves, then the master never meant to free her. So the words 'do not enslave her' must only mean 'don't work her hard', not 'free her'. Then why force the heirs to free her? The next step brings a different version of רבי יוחנן's ruling that avoids this problem, and אמימר later calls רב דימי's version a mistake (step 23).

keyTerms.meaning: Don't you agree?
Her children

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לְפָנָיו רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi said before him:
Rebbi, don't you agree
that her children are slaves?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לְפָנָיו רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב דימי's version of רבי יוחנן's ruling in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the heirs must free the maidservant
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If her children stay slaves, the master's words only meant to ease her work, not to free her, so forcing the heirs to free her makes no sense.

steps.title: Another version: give her something that makes her happy
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יהודה reports a different version of רבי יוחנן's ruling: if a dying master says his maidservant made him happy and should be made happy, the heirs are forced to do so.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב שמואל בר יהודה came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone said when he was dying, 'So-and-so my maidservant gave me satisfaction; let her be given satisfaction,' the court forces the heirs to give her satisfaction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of רבי יוחנן's ruling, with different wording from the dying master.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the master did not say 'do not enslave her' but 'do something that makes her happy.' The heirs must carry this out, and if only freedom would satisfy her, they must free her. This version avoids the problem raised by רבי אמי and רבי אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Satisfaction; something that makes a person happy
So-and-so (a woman)

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: When Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda came,
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who said at the time of his death,
"So-and-so, my maidservant, gave me satisfaction;
let satisfaction be done for her" —
we force the heirs
and they do for her what gives her satisfaction.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רבי יוחנן's ruling, different from רב דימי's version in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a dying master asks that his maidservant be given satisfaction, the heirs are forced to do it.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new ruling from a different person. It is the same רבי יוחנן, reported differently by a different messenger.

steps.title: Why must the heirs listen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the heirs are forced to follow the dying man's request.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next line by asking for the reason behind the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The property now belongs to the heirs, so it is not obvious why they must carry out the dead man's wishes. The גמרא wants the source of this obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why heirs are forced to carry out the dying man's instruction

steps.title: It is a מצוה to carry out the words of the dead
steps.stepSummary: The answer: it is a מצוה to carry out what a person instructed before he died.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a מצוה to carry out the words of the dead person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the heirs must listen because there is a מצוה to fulfill a dead person's instructions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This general principle, מצוה לקיים דברי המת, gives the court the power to force the heirs. It explains why the master's request about his maidservant has to be carried out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a מצוה to carry out the words of the dead

steps.whatToRemember: A dying person's instructions must be carried out by his heirs, because מצוה לקיים דברי המת.
steps.whyThisMatters: מצוה לקיים דברי המת is a basic principle used across many areas of inheritance and gifts in הלכה.

phrases.english: It is a מצוה to fulfill the words of the dead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The heirs are forced because it is a מצוה to fulfill the words of the dead.

steps.title: A slave whose master renounced him has no remedy
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules that a slave whose master was מפקיר him has no תקנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: If someone renounces ownership of his slave, that slave has no remedy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new ruling from אמימר about a master who renounces ownership of his slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the master is מפקיר the slave, the slave no longer belongs to him. But the slave is not yet fully free, so he still may not marry a Jewish woman. אמימר says there is no way to fix this situation.

keyTerms.meaning: One who renounces ownership (declares something ownerless)
A remedy, a way to fix the situation

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
One who renounces ownership of his slave,
that slave has no remedy.
phrases.notes: No remedy means he can never become fully free, so he can never marry a Jewish woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, the slave who was made ownerless.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave whose master was מפקיר him has no way to become fully free.

steps.title: Asking for the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the slave has no remedy.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why אמימר's ruling is true. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first it seems the master could simply write the slave a גט שחרור. The question asks what blocks that.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the master cannot fix the slave's status with a גט שחרור.

steps.title: The master owns only the prohibition, which cannot be transferred
steps.stepSummary: The master no longer owns the slave's body. All that is left is the איסורא, and that cannot be handed over.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not own the slave's body anymore. Only the prohibition remains with him, and he cannot transfer a prohibition to the slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the master cannot write a גט שחרור that works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט שחרור works by giving the slave ownership of himself. Here the master no longer owns the slave's body, so he has nothing to give. The only thing left is the איסורא (the ban on marrying a Jewish woman), and a ban is not something a person can transfer.

keyTerms.meaning: His body, meaning ownership of the slave himself
The prohibition (here, the ban on marrying a Jewish woman)
To transfer ownership

phrases.english: He does not own his body;
it is only the prohibition that remains with him,
and a prohibition he cannot transfer to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גט שחרור transfers ownership, but the master owns nothing transferable. Only the איסורא remains, and it cannot be given away.

steps.title: Challenge from the teaching that he needs a bill of freedom
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי cites רבי יוחנן and רב, who say such a slave goes free but needs a גט שחרור. That suggests a גט שחרור can help him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: But עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן, and רב חייא בר אבין said in the name of רב: In both this case and that case, the slave goes free, but he needs a bill of freedom!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges אמימר with a teaching from great earlier authorities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching says the ownerless slave 'needs' a גט שחרור. That sounds like a גט can be written for him and will work, which goes against אמימר's claim that he has no remedy.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes out to freedom
A bill of freedom given to a slave

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
But didn't Ulla say that Rabbi Yochanan said,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: and Rav Chiyya bar Avin said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה יָצָא לְחֵירוּת,
phrases.english: Both this one and that one go out to freedom,
phrases.notes: This one and that one are two cases discussed earlier in the גמרא. One of them is the master who renounces ownership of his slave.

phrases.english: and he needs a bill of freedom!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אמימר's ruling from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's ruling that the ownerless slave has no remedy.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the slave 'needs' a גט שחרור, then a גט must be available to him and must work.

steps.title: 'Needs' does not mean he can get one
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that the slave does need a גט, but there is no way for him to get one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He 'needs' one, but he has no remedy.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר defends his ruling by reading the word צריך narrowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching only tells us that without a גט he is not fully free. It does not say anyone is able to write him one. So the slave needs a גט, and he is still stuck.

keyTerms.meaning: Needs, requires

phrases.english: He said to him:
He 'needs' one, and yet he has no remedy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: צָרִיךְ וְאֵין לוֹ תַּקָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the cited source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Needs a גט שחרור' means a גט can be written and will work.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Needs' only means he lacks full freedom without one. In fact no one can write it, so he stays stuck.

steps.title: Second version: the master renounced the slave and then died
steps.stepSummary: Some report אמימר's ruling differently: it is about a master who was מפקיר his slave and then died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: אמימר said: If someone renounces ownership of his slave and then dies, that slave has no remedy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of אמימר's ruling, which adds that the master died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the master himself might still be able to write a גט. The problem only starts after he dies, when no one is left who can free the slave.

keyTerms.meaning: And he died

phrases.english: Some say: Ameimar said:
One who renounces ownership of his slave and dies,
that slave has no remedy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of אמימר's ruling from step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the master who was מפקיר his slave dies, no one can free the slave.

steps.title: Asking for the reason in the second version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the slave has no remedy after the master dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the second version. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We would expect the master's heir to take his place and write the גט. The question asks why the heir cannot.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the heir cannot free the slave.

steps.title: A prohibition cannot be inherited
steps.stepSummary: The master owned only the איסורא, and an איסורא does not pass to his son by inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not own the slave's body. Only the prohibition remains with him, and a prohibition he does not pass down to his son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the heir has nothing of the slave to work with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A son inherits his father's property. Here the father owned no property in the slave, only the איסורא, and that does not pass by inheritance. So the son has nothing, and he cannot write a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: To his son
Passes on as an inheritance

phrases.english: He does not own his body;
it is only the prohibition that remains with him,
and a prohibition he does not pass down to his son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The איסורא cannot be inherited, so the heir has no power to free the slave.

steps.title: Challenge from רב דימי's report of רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי cites רב דימי's report (step 9): heirs are forced to free a maidservant whom their father said not to enslave, even though they do not own her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: But when רב דימי came, he said that רבי יוחנן said...!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges the second version of אמימר's ruling from רב דימי's report earlier in the sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב דימי's case the father said 'do not enslave her', so the heirs never owned her. Even so, רבי יוחנן says they are forced to write her a גט שחרור. That shows heirs can free a slave they do not own, which goes against אמימר.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
But when Rav Dimi came,
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said...!
phrases.notes: He means the ruling from step 9: if a dying man says 'do not enslave her', the heirs are forced to write her a bill of freedom.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second version of אמימר's ruling (steps 19-21).
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that heirs cannot free a slave their father did not own.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In רב דימי's case the heirs never owned the maidservant, yet they are forced to free her. So heirs can free a slave they do not own.

steps.title: רב דימי's report is a mistake
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that רב דימי's report of רבי יוחנן is mistaken.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי's report is a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר rejects the source rather than answering it: he says רבי יוחנן never said it that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב דימי quoted רבי יוחנן wrongly, there is no real ruling that goes against אמימר. This fits with step 10, where רבי אמי and רבי אסי also found trouble with רב דימי's version.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistake, an error

phrases.english: That of Rav Dimi is a mistake.
phrases.notes: The speaker here is אמימר, even though the גמרא doesn't say his name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge in step 22 by rejecting the report.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the accuracy of the quoted source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן really ruled that heirs must free a maidservant they never owned.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב דימי's report is wrong, so it cannot be used against אמימר.

steps.title: If the mistake is only the wording, the point still stands
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks what exactly the mistake is. If it is only that the father didn't use words of freedom, then with words of freedom the heirs could free her, which still goes against אמימר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What is the mistake? That he didn't say it in words of freedom? Then if he had said it in words of freedom, would it indeed be so?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי presses אמימר: calling the report a mistake may not save his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The likely 'mistake' is that 'do not enslave her' is not proper freedom language (as in step 10). But that means that if the father had used freedom language, the heirs would be forced to write a גט, even though they never owned her. That still goes against אמימר.

keyTerms.meaning: In words of freeing a slave
So too, indeed it would be so

phrases.english: He said to him: What is the mistake?
That he did not say it in words of freedom?
Then if he had said it in words of freedom,
would it indeed be so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טָעוּתָא דְּלָא אַמְרַהּ בִּלְשׁוֹן שִׁחְרוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on אמימר's answer in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's claim that רב דימי's report is a mistake and so does not matter.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the only mistake is the wording, then with correct wording the heirs could still free her, so the problem for אמימר remains.

steps.title: אמימר follows רב שמואל בר יהודה's version
steps.stepSummary: אמימר says he holds like רב שמואל בר יהודה's version of רבי יוחנן, which is not about freedom at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I hold like the version of רב שמואל בר יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר ends the exchange by saying which version of רבי יוחנן he accepts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב שמואל בר יהודה's version (step 11), the father only asked the heirs to 'make her happy'. They fulfill this as a מצוה to keep a dying man's words. Nobody is freeing a slave, so this version says nothing about heirs freeing a slave they don't own, and אמימר's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: I hold, this is my opinion

steps.whatToRemember: אמימר holds that once a master is מפקיר his slave, the slave is stuck: neither the master's heirs nor (in the first version) the master himself can free him. He defends this by following רב שמואל בר יהודה's version of רבי יוחנן, which is about keeping a dying man's request, not about freeing a slave.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא כִּדְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לִי.
phrases.english: I hold like the version of Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda.
phrases.notes: That is step 11: the dying man said 'she made me happy, make her happy', with no talk of freeing her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנָא כִּדְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's push in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Choosing a different version of the cited teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's ruling is about freeing a maidservant, so it shows heirs can free a slave they don't own.
steps.terutzMaskana: The true version is about making her happy as a מצוה, not about freedom, so it does not contradict אמימר.

steps.title: רבינא sends freed-up slaves back to the sons of their first masters
steps.stepSummary: A town of slaves was sold to a non-Jew. After their last masters died, the slaves came to רבינא, and he told them to get a document of freedom from the sons of their original masters.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a town of slaves that was sold to a non-Jew. Their last masters died out, and the slaves came before רבינא. He told them: Go back to the sons of your first masters, and have them write you a document of freedom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a practical ruling by רבינא. This ruling will be challenged in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first masters had already sold these slaves away, so they no longer fully owned them. Even so, רבינא says the sons of those first masters can write a document of freedom. That is surprising, since heirs normally inherit only what their father owned.

keyTerms.meaning: A town or estate
Masters
The last ones / the first ones
A document of freedom (a גט שחרור)

phrases.english: There was a certain town of slaves
that was sold to a non-Jew.
Their last masters died out,
phrases.notes: The 'last masters' are the non-Jewish buyers.

phrases.english: and they came before Ravina.
He said to them: Go, turn back
to the sons of your first masters,
and let them write you a document of freedom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case that tests the earlier debate about whether heirs can free a slave their father no longer fully owned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The heirs of the original Jewish masters write a document of freedom for slaves who were sold to a non-Jew.

steps.title: The רבנן challenge רבינא from אמימר's rule
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן point out that אמימר ruled that a slave whose owner gave up ownership and then died has no fix, so how can heirs free these slaves?
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רבינא: But didn't אמימר say that if someone gives up ownership of his slave and then dies, that slave has no fix?
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן attack רבינא's ruling using אמימר's rule from earlier in the sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אמימר, once the owner lets go of the slave, his heirs inherit nothing they could use to free him. Selling the slave to a non-Jew is the same kind of case: the first masters no longer owned the slave's work. So their sons should not be able to write a document of freedom.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gives up ownership (makes it הפקר)
He has no fix, no way to be freed

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Ravina:
But didn't Ameimar say:
One who gives up ownership of his slave and dies,
that slave has no fix!
phrases.notes: He means nobody is left who can write him a document of freedom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's ruling in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's ruling that the sons of the first masters can free the slaves
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אמימר holds that heirs have no power over a slave their father had let go of, so the sons of the first masters cannot write a document of freedom.

steps.title: רבינא says he follows רב דימי
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that he holds like רב דימי's report of רבי יוחנן, which says heirs can be made to free such a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I hold like רב דימי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends himself by saying he follows a different opinion than אמימר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי reported that heirs are forced to free a maidservant whom their father had said should not be enslaved, even though the heirs do not own her. רבינא relies on that report, so in his view heirs can free a slave the father no longer fully owned.

keyTerms.meaning: I hold, this is my view

phrases.english: He said to them:
I hold like Rav Dimi.
phrases.notes: This is the report about the maidservant that רב אשי quoted in step 22.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבינא must hold like אמימר, so his ruling is wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבינא follows רב דימי's report, so heirs can free such slaves.

steps.title: The רבנן say רב דימי's report is a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reply that רב דימי's report is mistaken, which is the same thing אמימר said in step 23.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: רב דימי's report is a mistake!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן push back on רבינא's answer by rejecting the source he relies on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats אמימר's own defense from step 23. If רב דימי's report is wrong, רבינא has nothing left to stand on.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistake

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: דְּרַב דִּימִי טָעוּתָא הִיא!
phrases.english: They said to him: What Rav Dimi said is a mistake!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source רבינא relied on in step 28.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רב דימי's report of רבי יוחנן is a mistake, it cannot support רבינא's ruling.

steps.title: Even the mistake leaves room for רבינא
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks what the mistake is. At most, the father did not use words of freeing, so if words of freeing were used, the heirs can free the slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: What is the mistake? That the father did not say it in words of freeing. But if he did say it in words of freeing, then yes, the heirs can free the slave.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא shows that even if רב דימי made a mistake, it is only a small one, and it does not touch the main idea that heirs can free a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only 'mistake' could be about the wording the father used. That means that when the case does involve real freedom, the heirs can still write a document of freedom. So רבינא's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Words of freeing (a slave)
So indeed, yes that is true

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same argument רב אשי made against אמימר in step 24. רבינא is now using it to defend his own ruling.

phrases.english: He said to them: What is the mistake?
That he did not say it in words of freeing;
but if he had said it in words of freeing,
then so indeed!
phrases.notes: He means the heirs really would be able to write her a document of freedom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the claimed error
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If רב דימי erred, his whole report is useless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The error is only about wording. The basic rule, that heirs can free a slave when words of freeing were used, still stands.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבינא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like רבינא: the heirs of the original masters can write a document of freedom.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is like רבינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this story by deciding the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבינא's ruling holds up, the sons of the first masters can free slaves their father had sold to a non-Jew. אמימר's view does not decide the הלכה here.

keyTerms.meaning: And the practical ruling is

steps.whatToRemember: A master who sold his slave to a non-Jew no longer owns him, yet his heirs can still write the slave a document of freedom. The הלכה follows רבינא, not אמימר.

phrases.english: And the halakha is like Ravina.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the debate of steps 26 to 30.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The heirs of the original masters write a document of freedom, like רבינא.

steps.title: A partner gives his share of a half-freed slave to his minor son
steps.stepSummary: One partner freed his half of a jointly owned slave. The other partner, afraid the court would force him to free the rest, gave his share to his minor son. רב יוסף בריה דרבא sent this case to רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain slave belonged to two people. One of them freed his half. The other said: Now the רבנן will hear about me and make me lose him. So he went and transferred his share to his minor son. רב יוסף son of רבא sent the case to רב פפא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story and sets up a question that was sent to רב פפא. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave who is half free is normally forced to be freed fully by the court. The second partner tried to avoid that by giving his share to a child, because a child cannot be forced to free him. The question is whether this trick works.

keyTerms.meaning: He freed his half of him
They will cause a loss
He transferred ownership of him
A minor, a child under בר מצוה age

phrases.english: There was a certain slave who belonged to two people.
One of them got up
and freed his half.
The other one said:
Now the Rabbis will hear about me
and make me lose him;
phrases.notes: He is afraid the court will force him to free his half too.

phrases.english: so he went and transferred him to his minor son.
Rav Yosef son of Rava sent this case
before Rav Pappa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about freeing slaves, separate from the רבינא story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What to do when a partner gives his share of a half-freed slave to his minor son to escape being forced to free him.

steps.title: רב פפא turns the trick back on the father
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers with פסוקים: as he did, so will be done to him. A child is drawn to money, so the court will appoint a guardian for him. The plan continues in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back to him: 'As he did, so shall be done to him; his dealing will come back on his own head.' We know that a child's mind is drawn to money, so we will appoint a guardian for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא begins his answer. He says the father's trick will backfire, and he starts laying out how the court will handle it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father used his child to dodge the court, so the court will use the child's situation against him. Since a child likes money, the court will appoint a guardian who can deal with the slave on the child's behalf. The details of the plan continue in the next part of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: His dealing, what he did
We know it as an established fact
A child
A guardian appointed to manage a child's property

phrases.english: He sent back to him:
"As he has done, so shall be done to him,
his dealing shall return upon his own head."
phrases.notes: This mixes language from two פסוקים: ויקרא 24:19 and עובדיה 1:15.

phrases.english: We know about a child
that his mind is drawn to money;
so we appoint a guardian for him,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question sent in step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The father's trick will backfire. The court appoints a guardian for the child, using the fact that a child is drawn to money. The plan continues in the next lines.
